newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian inflation in February slows to 2.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Italian inflation in February slows to 2.4 percent.

text.p: Italy's major measure of inflation, the consumer price index (CPI), slipped to an annual rate of 2.4 percent in February from 2.6 percent in January, Italy's National Statistic Office (ISTAT) reported on Tuesday.
The official data was in line with market expectations and is the lowest CPI inflation rate in Italy since May 1969.
Inflation has been generally falling over the last year. The annual CPI rate stood at 5.0 percent in February 1996.
Provisional figures from 11 Italian cities in late February had pointed towards an annual rate of 2.4 percent.
Many economists see the falling trend in inflation leading to further cuts in Italy's 6.75 percent discount rate in the next two to three months once a 1997 mini-budget has passed through parliament.
The monthly CPI index in February rose by 0.1 percent after a 0.2 percent rise in January and a 0.3 percent increase in February 1996.
